key_insight: UniSlider makes image-editing sliders behave more like how humans perceive change: equal slider movement produces more consistent, predictable visual change. Instead of treating the slider as a raw strength parameter, it remaps it to avoid dead zones, abrupt jumps, and partial reversals.
problem_solved: Current generative image-editing sliders are usually just linear or ad hoc rescalings of model strength parameters, which do not correspond well to perceptual change. This leads to uninformative ranges, sudden transformations, and unstable editing behavior.
method: Remaps the underlying edit strength into a perceptually uniform slider space.
Balances the slider response so visual change progresses more smoothly and consistently across the full range.
Improves the usability of continuous image editing by making slider motion better match user expectations.
impact: For practitioners, this means more controllable and intuitive image editing interfaces with less trial-and-error. It can make generative editing tools easier to use for both interactive workflows and downstream applications that need stable, fine-grained control.

paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral
